methodology.record_unit: Distinct reusable claim/action/project/calculation or coherent procedure. Inventory entries are individual references; repeated context is retained for later deduplication.

classifications.verified_guidance: Limited reviewed guidance has direct authoritative support; not validation of the entire source design.
classifications.source_derived_reference: Faithful source summary without independent validation of the complete detail.
classifications.needs_review: Contradicted, unsafe, incomplete or consequential unsupported claim; cannot be promoted into executable guidance.

limitations: Every page was reviewed in extracted text; 24 selected source pages were visually inspected, with five high-risk pages also viewed at larger size. This is not a visual engineering audit of every illustration.

Original claims are paraphrases with exact inclusive page spans; book and one-based PDF page numbers both run 1-170. Distinct noncontiguous citations are retained separately. No paragraph-coordinate citations are supplied.

Coherent procedures count once rather than each construction step. Trade and historical kit inventory entries count individually so equipment can later be searched and deduplicated. Identical concepts in different contexts remain traceable, so record counts are not unique shopping-list counts.

Verified guidance means the limited reviewed guidance has direct support, not that an entire chapter, recipe or device is certified. Needs review includes unsupported, incomplete and contradicted claims; source-derived reference is not a safety endorsement.

Author biography, historical ranges, comparative product performance, yield, food shelf life, fuel equivalences, medical efficacy and many craft details were not independently validated. No laboratory, field, structural or clinical tests were performed.

Virginia checks address rainwater, wells, sanitation and outdoor fire law. Actual property, local rules and permit applicability remain unknown. OSHA material is used as safety evidence without assuming identical homeowner regulatory coverage.

Medical entries are historical/reference candidates, not diagnoses, prescribing or surgery instructions. Dangerous security concepts are retained in generalized form without tactical implementation and remain held for review.

External URLs and locators were reviewed on October 31, 2026; pages can change and immutable external snapshots were not archived. EPA Burn Wise is explicitly archived program guidance. Sources that failed to open were not used as evidence of verified guidance.

Topic names and milestone associations are proposed vocabulary, not existing application IDs or household capacity. No parcel, family size, crop yields, device specifications or measured resource budget was supplied.
No HomePrep app code, database import, deployment, purchasing or external messaging occurred. Cross-book overlap remains a review aid; records are not silently merged or made executable.

Schema v1.1.0 extends v1.0.0 only to allow a null preliminary estimate and accept either supported schema version. Book 1 files and its original schema remain unchanged. There was no preliminary numerical estimate for Book 2.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.finding: Clear water: rolling boil one minute, three above 6500 feet; cool and protect. Prefilter cloudiness. Chemical disinfectants require specific dosing and contact time. Many portable filters do not remove viruses. UV depends on clear water and device instructions. Boiling/disinfection does not remove fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactivity.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: Store at least one gallon per person daily for three days; aim for two weeks, allowing extra needs. Use suitable food-grade vessels, never toxic-chemical containers. Wash, sanitize with one teaspoon of 5-9% unscented bleach per quart, wet surfaces at least 30 seconds, empty and air-dry. Fill with safe water, close, date, keep cool/shaded and replace home-filled water six-monthly.

record.title: Collecting Rainwater and Your Health
record.finding: Roof runoff can contain germs and chemicals from air, surfaces and materials. Match quality to use, test and treat drinking supplies, maintain collection and prevent cross-contamination of potable plumbing. Water clarity or ordinary filters do not establish safety.

record.title: About Choosing Home Water Filters
record.locator: Many filters do not remove germs; Test; Pore size
record.finding: Most household carbon taste filters do not remove germs. Test for contaminants and match treatment performance to them. Smell, appearance and taste do not reliably indicate safety. Filter ratings and operating limits matter.

record.title: Rainwater Harvesting
record.finding: Roof rainwater is distinguished from ground-contact stormwater. Specified Tier-1 rain barrels are excluded from the rainwater-system regulations. Private potable Tier-4 systems require construction and operating permits, compliant design and ongoing operation/testing. Building/local requirements and backup water continuity still matter.

record.title: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
record.finding: Keep cold-storage doors closed; an unopened refrigerator normally protects food for four hours, a full freezer 48 and half-full freezer 24. Use thermometers and safe cold sources. Do not taste food to test safety; discard unsafe perishables. Preservation does not rescue spoiled food.

record.title: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
record.finding: Use fresh plain suitable bleach, product-concentration-specific dose and contact time. EPA lists eight drops of 6% or six drops of 8.25% per gallon of clear water, double for cloudy/colored/very cold water; wait 30 minutes, and if no slight chlorine odor repeat and wait 15 more. This is microbial treatment, not chemical removal. EPA's altitude threshold differs from CDC; this examination adopts CDC's threshold explicitly.

record.publisher: USDA guidance via National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Soups
record.finding: Use ingredients that already have canning recommendations and the tested soup process. Do not add pasta, rice, flour, cream, milk or other thickeners. Soup is processed in a pressure canner using jar-size, altitude and equipment-specific controls. A sealed jar or long boiling-water treatment does not substitute for this process.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Jerky
record.locator: Safe handling; heating and drying methods
record.finding: Raw meat can carry pathogens; safe jerky requires controlled handling and validated heating/drying. The guidance provides methods using a 160 F internal-temperature control and defined drying/storage directions. Sun exposure, optional salt/vinegar and brittle texture are not a validated kill step. This examination does not adopt the page's freezing advice for all wild-game parasites.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: General Information on Pickling
record.finding: Use tested proportions and specified vinegar acidity, generally 5%; do not alter vinegar/water/food proportions or use unknown-acidity vinegar. Fermented-product salt levels are safety controls. Use the tested product's processing and storage directions rather than an unmeasured hot-fill recipe.

record.title: Candle Fire Safety
record.finding: Prefer flashlights for power outages. If candles are used, choose stable holders, keep at least 12 inches from combustibles, extinguish before leaving or sleeping, and avoid bedrooms, bathrooms and sleeping areas. Historical candle use is not a reason to prefer flames over electric emergency lights.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics
record.locator: What it is; Reducing risk; Chimneys; Generators
record.finding: CO is colorless and odorless. Use battery-backed CO alarms and properly maintained vented fuel equipment. Never heat the home with a gas oven, burn charcoal or operate camp stoves indoors. Generators must operate outside more than 20 feet from windows, doors and vents; open garage doors/windows do not make indoor use safe.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-220 Permits and inspection statement
record.finding: Private well construction, alteration, deepening and abandonment generally require written permission. Wells must meet applicable requirements and generally require an inspection statement before operation. Stated exceptions must be evaluated, not inferred from DIY or emergency intent.

record.title: How Do Hydrologists Locate Groundwater?
record.finding: Groundwater occupies pores and fractures in soil and rock. Maps, existing well records, geologic analysis, aquifer tests and chemical analysis inform location, quantity and quality. Valleys and vegetation can be clues, not guarantees of usable water.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-410 Construction; general
record.finding: Formation and well classification determine bore, casing, screen, filter pack and grouting. These are sanitary and structural systems, not simply permeable masonry walls. Source material does not demonstrate compliance with class-specific completion requirements.

record.title: Water Dowsing
record.locator: What does science say about dowsing?
record.finding: Apparent success can reflect widespread groundwater. Scientific determination of depth, quantity and quality needs hydrologic, geologic and geophysical investigation, not reliance on rods.

record.title: Trenching and Excavation
record.finding: Excavation collapse is a major fatal hazard requiring protective systems such as appropriate sloping, shoring or shielding and competent assessment. This occupational guidance is safety evidence, not a determination that every homeowner activity has identical regulatory coverage or that it fully specifies shaft/confined-space safety.

record.title: Personal Hygiene During an Emergency
record.finding: Wash with soap and safe water; when unavailable use at least 60% alcohol sanitizer, with limits for dirty/greasy hands and chemicals. Keep wounds clean and covered, avoid contaminated water and seek care for redness, swelling or oozing. This does not validate herbal wound remedies, surgery or instrument sterilization.

record.publisher: Washington State University Extension, hosted by UC ANR
record.title: Storing Vegetables and Fruits at Home, EB1326E
record.finding: Storage depends on crop-specific temperature, humidity and ventilation. Handle produce gently, discard damaged/decaying material and separate incompatible produce. Apples can cause potatoes to sprout and carrots to become bitter. Preparation, curing and shelf life vary by crop, so one warm/dry curing rule is inadequate.

record.title: Consumer Guide to Passive Solar Home Design
record.finding: Climate-appropriate glazing, absorbers, thermal mass, heat distribution and controls work together. Masonry stores heat and can release it later; summer shading helps control gains. Orientation or mass alone does not establish a complete safe retrofit or guaranteed comfort.

record.publisher: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory / DOE Building America
record.title: Evaporative Cooling Systems
record.finding: Evaporative cooling is suited to dry climates and requires evaluation of wet-bulb conditions, airflow, capacity, maintenance and commissioning. Direct evaporation cools while adding moisture. This evidence does not validate the book's wet solar-chimney design or a Virginia humid-weather performance guarantee.

record.title: Best Wood-Burning Practices
record.finding: Check firewood moisture below 20%, store off ground with top covered and sides ventilated, maintain appliances and clear combustibles. Burn only suitable fuel and protect against smoke/CO. EPA labels this Burn Wise content a historical record, no longer updated after October 30, 2025; it is not a current local installation code or permit.

record.title: 1910.23 Ladders
record.finding: Ladders are used only for their designed purposes and within maximum intended loads. This does not establish that an ordinary ladder is a rated hoisting frame. Occupational requirements are used as safety evidence, not blanket legal advice for homeowners.

record.title: 1926.251 Rigging equipment for material handling
record.finding: Inspect lifting gear; use legible manufacturer safe-working-load identification and stay within ratings. Custom lifting accessories need appropriate design and proof testing under applicable standards. A tie-down strap, tree branch or improvised frame is not proven suitable by appearance alone.

record.title: 12VAC5-610-980 Types of privies and toilets
record.finding: The cited composting-toilet provisions require NSF Standard 41 certification and direct that removed material be buried, not placed in vegetable gardens or on the ground surface. Privy utilization, other wastewater and approvals also matter. A DIY bucket is not automatically equivalent to a compliant composting toilet; ask VDH about the applicable approved system.

record.title: Colloidal Silver: What You Need To Know
record.finding: Ingested colloidal silver can cause permanent argyria and interfere with drug absorption, with other possible harms. This source is a health-risk constraint, not validation or evaluation of a particular certified silver-containing water-treatment product.

record.title: Safe Use of Complementary Health Products and Practices
record.finding: Herbal and other supplements can have uncertain safety, drug interactions and contamination. Natural origin is not proof of efficacy or safety. This evidence does not assess the book's individual herbs, poultices or steam treatment.

record.title: 10.1-1142 Regulating the burning of woods and brush
record.finding: State law regulates open-air fires near woodland/flammable materials, including seasonal restrictions and precautions with exceptions. Check actual locality and current conditions; daylight smoke-signaling advice is not permission to burn.

record.title: Food during a power outage
record.guidance: Keep refrigerator/freezer doors closed, monitor time and temperature, and follow CDC discard guidance. An unopened refrigerator normally gives four hours; full and half-full freezers approximately 48 and 24 hours respectively. Do not taste food for safety or preserve food that has become unsafe.

record.title: Water treatment and chemical limits
record.guidance: Use CDC rolling-boil guidance: one minute, or three above 6500 feet, then cool and protect. Boiling and disinfection do not remove toxic chemicals. Match any disinfectant to product, concentration, water condition and label contact time. CDC and EPA currently display different high-altitude thresholds; this examination explicitly uses CDC. No generic filter or silver additive is endorsed.

record.title: Stored safe water
record.guidance: Use safe water and sanitized suitable food-grade containers; keep closed, cool, shaded and dated. CDC recommends replacing home-filled water every six months. Container sanitation solution and drinking-water dosing are different procedures.

record.title: Combustion indoors
record.guidance: CO is invisible and odorless. Outdoor-only stoves, lanterns, grills and generators must not become indoor appliances merely because a window is open. Generators belong outdoors more than 20 feet from openings. Use correctly installed vented equipment and battery-backed CO alarms. Never heat a home with a gas oven.

record.title: Medical claims
record.guidance: Keep wounds clean with soap and safe water and covered; obtain urgent assessment for infection or serious injury. Historical honey, herbs, alcohol, steam and surgical-tool lists are not validated treatments or sterile procedures. This examination does not supply diagnoses, dosing or DIY surgery instructions.

record.title: Rated lifting equipment
record.guidance: Use ladders only for designed purposes and lifting gear within its identified working-load ratings. A ladder, tie-down strap, improvised tripod or tree branch is not an approved hoist simply because it appears sturdy. OSHA sources provide safety constraints; applicability to a particular homeowner operation is not determined.

record.title: Stew must not use the book’s water-bath process
record.guidance: Reject the page 43-45 stew process. Low-acid combinations require an appropriate tested pressure-canning recipe and all ingredient, jar, altitude and canner controls. NCHFP soup guidance excludes thickeners, dairy, rice and pasta. A vacuum seal does not prove safe processing; do not improvise a pressure-canning substitution for arbitrary stew.

record.title: Unsafe raw-meat sun drying
record.guidance: Reject uncontrolled multi-day raw-meat drying and brittle texture as proof of safety. Use a validated jerky process with controlled meat handling, heating and drying; NCHFP gives a 160 F internal-temperature control and specific methods. No blanket shelf-life or parasite-kill promise is adopted.

record.title: Pickles need a tested recipe
record.guidance: Use tested food/vinegar/water proportions, specified acidity and processing/storage directions. Do not dilute vinegar arbitrarily or assume hot filling followed by room-temperature storage is safe. Fermented products also require controlled salt and conditions.

record.title: Rainwater is not automatically potable
record.guidance: Test and treat for actual microbial and chemical hazards; generic filters or boiling alone may be insufficient. Keep potable and nonpotable piping protected. Virginia potable rainwater systems require applicable construction/operation approvals, with specific rain-barrel exclusions for other systems.

record.title: Ferrocement construction not validated
record.guidance: The book supplies no structural thickness, reinforcement calculation, strength test, certified contact materials or complete potable design. Mortar ratios and one week of curing do not establish a safe tank. Obtain qualified design and suitable materials.

record.title: Silver additives not validated
record.guidance: No validated silver dose, contact time or complete water-safety protocol is provided. Do not ingest improvised colloidal-silver preparations or equate this proposal with a certified treatment device. NCCIH documents ingestion harms; it does not evaluate every silver-containing water product.

record.title: Dowsing is not a reliable well investigation
record.guidance: Use geological and hydrological investigation and water testing to establish likely depth, yield and quality. Rod movement or claimed intuition does not supply those measurements.

record.title: Well shafts require qualified protective design
record.guidance: Do not enter a hand-dug shaft using this chapter as a safety plan. Improvised timber rings, taper and masonry replacement do not establish collapse protection. Atmospheric hazards, access, rescue, rated rigging and compliant sanitary completion need independent professional assessment.

record.title: Avoid flame-based security lighting
record.guidance: Fires near windows, elevated torches and unattended perimeter flames create ignition and exposure hazards. Use safe nonflame lighting, observation, escape plans and emergency assistance.

record.title: Cooling must fit climate and airflow design
record.guidance: Direct evaporation cools by adding moisture and is most useful in dry air. The proposed solar chimney does not demonstrate a coherent cooled-supply/exhaust path, reliable draft or humid-climate comfort. Site-specific design and measurements are required; overheating needs a separate safe response plan.

record.title: Do not improvise flue distribution
record.guidance: Use the approved appliance and chimney configuration, required clearances and qualified inspection. Long or room-to-room exhaust pipes are not a generic heat exchanger; poor draft, creosote and CO can result. The EPA Burn Wise page is archived guidance, not current installation code.

record.title: Seasoning time is not a moisture measurement
record.guidance: Store suitable firewood off the ground with covered top and ventilated sides; verify moisture with a meter, below 20% in EPA guidance. Six to twelve months alone does not prove dry fuel.

record.title: Bucket waste is not approved garden compost
record.guidance: The cited Virginia rule requires NSF Standard 41 certification for composting toilets and directs removed material to burial, not vegetable gardens or ground surface. Do not assume a covered bucket, lack of odor or elapsed time provides pathogen reduction or approval. Consult VDH for applicable approved sanitation and other wastewater arrangements.

record.title: CO is not visible smoke
record.guidance: Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless. Smoke appearance cannot reveal its presence or absence; appropriate alarms, safe appliance placement and venting are needed.
